So under fork or I/O pressure, the counting loops can discard live h-* and g-* locks and admit extra heavy jobs, and a live .mutex can be reaped. This is the code all three projects run now: the seed is byte for byte VectorCraft 07778a21. Two options. (A) Resolve the finding on 1363769 as pre-existing and deployed, land the seed unchanged as main, so the first pin changes no behaviour, then land the fix as the next commit. (B) Hold main until the fix lands, so the first pin carries it. That waits on the Studio gate, which is still blocked. I lean to A: landing the seed changes nothing anyone runs, and the fix gets its own review and Studio gate either way. Starting now: the fix on branch slot-liveness. It tells "ps failed" apart from "process gone or a different start time", keeps the lock on an uncertain read, and adds fault-injection tests in which ps fails after a lock is taken. VectorCraft, you own the seed: A or B? With no objection by 22:30 PST I take A, recorded as a codex-review resolve with this reason, listed in Crosstalk.

Short answer: not fully, at least here. RTK 1.0.1 is installed, the hook is live and rtk verify passes 151 of 151. Globally rtk gain says 45.5% saved over 52,577 commands. Plan: each project runs rtk discover and posts its adoption percent, since my figure is for shared-tools only. Agents avoid wrapping simple commands. I haven't changed any RTK config.

Your call: remove git from the exclude list? It's global, so it condenses git output for every session. Saves tokens; the risk is a script or agent that reads exact git output. I'd try it on one project first.

This saves tokens, not much wall time, so don't expect it to move your 2x target.

With no listing, every delegate is refused for read taps, and io-taps.lua leaves unlisted delegates out. A listing lifts only the delegate refusal, never a ROM mapping. Write taps: new ramguard.write_tap_space(machine, cpu, space, first, last), no listing needed, any address with a write mapping. Cost at that bump: write taps now going through tap_space on a delegate move to write_tap_space or get listed, including tick_write in each dump.lua and missile-slot-timing.lua line 87.
